stem: An isoquant defines the combinations of inputs that yield different levels of output.
explain: Correct! An isoquant defines the combinations of inputs that yield the same level of output.

stem: The marginal rate of technical substitution (MRTS) is _______.
choices: the absolute value of the slope of the isoquant
the rate at which a producer can substitute between two outputs and maintain the same level of input
the rate at which a producer can substitute between two inputs and maintain the same level of output
both the rate at which a producer can substitute between two inputs and maintain the same level of output, and the absolute value of the slope of the isoquant
explain: Correct! The MRTS is the rate at which a producer can substitute between two inputs and maintain the same level of output. It is also the absolute value of the slope of the isoquant.

stem: Isoquants closer to the origin are associated with higher levels of output.
explain: Correct! Isoquants that are closer to the origin are associated with lower levels of output.

stem: The slope of an isocost line is equal to _____.
explain: Correct! The slope of an isocost line is equal to -w/r.

stem: An isocost line is drawn with capital (K) on the vertical axis. Its y-intercept is C/r and its slope is -w/r. If the price of capital (r) increases, what happens to the isocost line?
choices: The y-intercept will decrease and the slope will increase in magnitude.
The y-intercept will increase and the slope will increase in magnitude.
The y-intercept will increase and the slope will decrease in magnitude.
The y-intercept will decrease and the slope will decrease in magnitude.
explain: Correct! The y-intercept is C/r and the slope is -w/r. When r rises, the y-intercept falls and the slope becomes less steep (it decreases in magnitude).
